title: TP/PP warmup and KV-aware saturation sweep for cross-node throughput regression detection
creator: Aisha Mendes
description: Objective: Build a reproducible benchmark harness that stresses tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) configurations across 2-8 node clusters and surfaces regression signals in tokens/sec and p95 latency under realistic warmup dynamics and prefix KV-cache effects. The harness must emulate mixed-length traffic, microburst arrivals, and persistent KV cache reuse to detect regressions caused by kernel selection changes, batching policy regressions, and cross-node RPC variability.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible end-to-end runs for at least 6 TP/PP topology permutations (e.g., TP=2/4, PP=1/2/4) on 2 and 4 node setups
Time-series outputs for tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail-jitter, and KV-hit ratio written to the canonical benchmark S3 prefix
Automated regression detector that computes rolling baselines (7-run median) and flags >=10% drop in sustained tokens/sec or >=20% increase in p95 with annotated stack traces/commit info
Runbook documenting how to reproduce an observed regression locally and which artifacts to attach to a PR (traces, kernel selection logs, batching histograms)
tasks: Design traffic generator with mixed sequence lengths and microburst Poisson arrivals
Add KV-emulation layer to warm and persist prefix caches across requests
Instrument client and runtime to emit per-request tokens/generated, backend kernel choice, and KV hit/miss
Create orchestration recipes for 2-/4-/8-node clusters in CI rig and on-prem lab
Build regression detector (simple stats + nonparametric test) and alert rule integration for Slack/Incidents
Validate against model v1.12 and v1.14 variants and record baseline profiles
test_plan: Baseline sweep: run 3 cold->warm cycles per topology, collect baseline medians
Saturation sweep: gradually increase concurrency until throughput plateaus or p95 exceeds SLO
Microburst probe: inject 100ms bursts at 90th percentile arrival rates and record tail impact
KV-stress: vary prefix-reuse from 0% to 90% to measure cache-sensitive throughput deltas
Cross-node variance: repeat runs with network perturbation (added 2-5ms RTT) to measure routing sensitivity
results_summary: Initial baselines established for model-v1.12 on 4-node TP=2 PP=2 produced 1.9M tokens/sec sustained with p95=78ms after warmup. Enabling aggressive continuous batching increased tokens/sec by 18% but widened p95 by 14ms in microburst scenarios. KV warmup shows a non-linear benefit: moving from 10% to 70% prefix reuse reduced p95 by 22% and boosted tokens/sec by 12% on TP-heavy topologies.
regressions_observed: Run 2026-03-10 03:14: kernel selection path change in runtime@main caused 12% tokens/sec drop on TP=4 PP=1 under high sequence-length variance
PR #3321 introduced eager-batching tweak that raised p95 by ~18ms in microburst tests; reverted for immediate mitigation
